propositions: Duplicated business logic exists in 2-7 locations across the codebase (sidecar keying, git_adapter by-path loads, pytest --basetemp, comment key/send, compaction) causing fixes to land in one copy while twins remain broken.

Each consolidation child must collapse one duplicated computation into a single shared module, preserve all current pinned behavior verified by named tests, and land with a construct-uniqueness guard asserting exactly one implementation exists.

Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 measure proxies that correct consolidation work legitimately violates: AC2 requires tests-only-additions but consolidation must delete duplicated test copies; AC3 requires net-negative non-test lines but extraction necessarily costs more in documented owner module than recovered from emptied call sites.

The epic has 23 children total: 13 consolidation children collapsing duplicate logic (measured +2449 net lines across non-test files, contradicting AC3 goal) and 9 hardening children adding behavior with separate acceptance criteria.

AC2 and AC3 were written before any child landed and fail empirically on merged work despite correct consolidation behavior; they require restatement to measure actual guarantees (one implementation per construct, no pinned behavior change) rather than unsatisfiable proxies.
